mentions.name: Ember
mentions.description: This day planner app treats schedules as dynamic instead of fixed: when a task is moved or its duration changes, everything after it shifts later and flows around fixed items like meetings, avoiding manual replanning. It is currently web + Capacitor and is being rebuilt as a native Kotlin app, with full-duplex voice models being explored so tasks can be added or moved by conversing with an agent.
mentions.problem: Most planners treat your schedule as fixed, so the moment a meeting runs long or a task takes twice as long, the plan is wrong and you either fix it by hand or give up on it.
mentions.source_excerpt:
For the past two years I've been working on my day planner app Ember.

Most planners treat your schedule as fixed, so the moment a meeting runs long or a task takes twice as long, the plan is wrong and you either fix it by hand or give up on it. In Ember, if you move a task or change how long it takes, everything after it shifts later, and it flows around fixed things like meetings.
mentions.author: hhhkm
